title: Pin Hyprland to the NVIDIA card when it is the only GPU beside a firmware framebuffer
head: 11e784239903
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Render-only DRM cards are mistaken for extra display GPUs, so the fix is silently skipped
leads.consequence: The Linux DRM core allocates cardN nodes even for DRIVER_RENDER without DRIVER_MODESET. With simpledrm, NVIDIA and a vgem card (whose sysfs parent has driver faux_driver), the helper exits 1 with empty stdout, so both Lua configs leave Aquamarine's autodetection in place, despite Aquamarine rejecting vgem as non-KMS. The original framebuffer failure can recur on a machine with a render-only provider; next config evaluation still skips the pin until that provider disappears. The same class includes v3d, panfrost, lima and etnaviv. Classify only KMS-capable display devices as 'other GPU', not every cardN with a non-NVIDIA driver.
leads.triage: Opus follow-up: render-only cards do make the helper skip the pin; missed case, not a regression; irrelevant for x86

leads.summary: Two NVIDIA display cards select just the first and discard the other's outputs
leads.consequence: If card1 and card2 are distinct NVIDIA DRM display cards beside simpledrm, both satisfy the 'nvidia' arm but only card1 is emitted. Aquamarine treats AQ_DRM_DEVICES as an exclusive list, so outputs attached to card2 are missing when both GPUs would otherwise be scanned. The same result repeats on compositor restart. Either refuse to pin on multiple NVIDIA cards or emit all NVIDIA cards deliberately in the explicit list after validating their capability.

leads.summary: Both Lua configs overwrite an administrator's explicit AQ_DRM_DEVICES selection
leads.consequence: On the detected topology, both configs call hl.env unconditionally even if a user or UWSM has set a custom AQ_DRM_DEVICES list. A real Lua run with inherited '/dev/dri/card9:/dev/dri/card1' instead calls hl.env('AQ_DRM_DEVICES', '/dev/dri/card1'); Aquamarine then discards all other specified cards. Another open PR, #8786, rewrites a user's UWSM by-path selection before startup, but this config subsequently replaces it. Preserve a deliberately set value, or document an explicit opt-out; verify correct precedence on reload as well.

leads.summary: Greeter command breaks when OMARCHY_PATH contains an apostrophe
leads.consequence: Unlike the session's o.shell_quote, the SDDM config wraps OMARCHY_PATH in raw single quotes. A legitimate path containing an apostrophe makes the shell report an unmatched quote, io.popen reads no card and the greeter gets no pin. The failing compositor path is retried unchanged on subsequent starts. Shell-escape the path the same way the session does or execute an argv vector without a shell. This only applies when the greeter has a non-default OMARCHY_PATH.

leads.summary: #13659 can nest the pin under its active-display gate, defeating it when only the simpledrm connector is reported connected
leads.consequence: The independently proposed #13659 wraps the whole NVIDIA block, including the new pin after a clean file-level merge, in omarchy-hw-nvidia-active-display. The simpledrm Unknown connector is connected even without a monitor, making that detector refuse its boot_vga fallback if the NVIDIA display connector has not yet reported connected. Synthetic merged run produces no AQ_DRM_DEVICES in that shape; when NVIDIA connector is connected the positive control pins card1. This is conditional on #13659 merging and the NVIDIA connector status at config time; keep the DRM pin outside the new GL/VA active-display gate when reconciling those PRs. GitHub currently reports #13659 CONFLICTING with base for other changes, so do not equate the source-derived file merge with a whole-PR merge.
leads.triage: stale premise: #13659 at 61b75ae no longer changes nvidia.lua; Opus follow-up confirms pin stays outside the gate

leads.summary: Related open PRs have unresolved overlapping hunks requiring the DRM pin to be preserved manually
leads.consequence: Source-derived three-way merges against the other PRs' own common ancestors contain conflict markers for #9483 and #7851 (session NVIDIA config), and #6896, #10574 and #7501 (SDDM greeter prelude). The latter three are individually MERGEABLE against current quattro but cannot be combined with this PR's greeter prelude automatically; choosing their side of the conflict drops the pin, choosing this side drops keyboard/DPMS/scale behaviour. #9483 and #7851 already report CONFLICTING with base. Reconcile those hunks with both features and run the respective fixture suites before merging both branches; a conflict is not a runtime regression while unmerged.
leads.triage: verified: #9483/#7851 (Opus) and #6896/#10574/#7501 greeter conflicts (coordinator git merge-file, Opus merge-tree)

leads.summary: The tests can pass without any Lua pin, and do not check the helper's negative exit code
leads.consequence: The new suite calls only the detector; removing hl.env('AQ_DRM_DEVICES', card) from both configs leaves its assertions unchanged, and the existing NVIDIA Lua test at the base tip prints only NVD_BACKEND, LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME and GLX. Both the current-base test and new suite pass while the pin is absent, leaving the intended login fix untested. Separately, a plausible detector mutation replacing negative 'exit 1' with 'exit 0' passes all seven new cases because assert_card discards the status. Add synthetic-sysfs tests that evaluate both Lua configs and assert hl.env, plus assert the helper's exit status on negative controls.

leads.summary: The EFI and VESA 'DRM card' fixtures are not produced by stock Linux
leads.consequence: The test asserts that a synthetic card1 with efi-framebuffer is a DRM primary card, and the helper advertises efidrm/vesadrm beside simpledrm. At Linux v7.2, efifb and vesafb register fbdev framebuffers, not DRM cardN nodes; simpledrm alone registers such a KMS card. The EFI case therefore tests a sysfs topology not supplied by those drivers and gives false assurance about claimed coverage. Replace this case with a real DRM producer or narrow the comment/claim and keep the simpledrm control.
leads.triage: wrong: efidrm/vesadrm are DRM drivers in Linux v7.2 (drivers/gpu/drm/sysfb/, gh api contents at v7.2)

leads.summary: #9063's debug warning will misidentify this dynamic card pin as an unsafe hard-coded pin
leads.consequence: If both PRs merge and debug is launched as a Hyprland child, the computed '/dev/dri/card1' is in the child's environment. #9063 unconditionally prints 'pins /dev/dri/cardN, which rotates across reboots'; that diagnosis is inappropriate for a cardN re-detected from sysfs on each startup. It can misdirect troubleshooting even though this PR avoided a persistent numbered pin. Make the diagnostic distinguish a static user config assignment from a dynamic compositor-generated value, or qualify the warning. This concerns future combined diagnostic output, not the current compositor startup.

limits: All device-response tests ran with synthetic sysfs inside review.py, no NVIDIA/MUX GPU, SDDM service or live Hyprland/Aquamarine compositor was available; source-derived Aquamarine/kernel evidence supports conditional consequences, not a measured compositor crash.

Merged-result tests were run for current quattro tip and #13659 file-level composition only; conflict-bearing combinations #9483/#7851/#6896/#10574/#7501 cannot be executed without a manual conflict resolution choice, and there is no proof of the eventual resolver's choice.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** With two NVIDIA cards beside a firmware framebuffer, only the first is pinned, so per Aquamarine source the other card's outputs would stay dark.

### A second NVIDIA card is excluded from `AQ_DRM_DEVICES`

The helper keeps the first `nvidia` card and ignores a second one: simpledrm plus two `nvidia` cards prints `/dev/dri/card1`, exit 0. **Impact:** per Aquamarine source (not tested on hardware), only listed cards are opened at startup, so the second card's outputs stay dark.

**Suggested change:** Pin only when exactly one NVIDIA card is present, or print all of them joined with `:` and widen both Lua matches.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 11e7842)</summary>

Reviewed head: `11e7842399030ad5affee4dc1214fb4272632e89`. The same result was also recorded on a trial merge with `quattro` at `8b4eae66da2938ba9559f103b18dbf85cdf28a70`.

Append this case to `test/shell.d/hw-nvidia-drm-card-test.sh`. It uses the file's own `write_drm` and `hw_nvidia_drm_card` helpers and accepts either possible fix: pinning every NVIDIA card, or not pinning at all.

```bash
write_drm card0:simple-framebuffer card1:nvidia card2:nvidia
actual=$(hw_nvidia_drm_card) || actual=""
[[ -z $actual || $actual == *"/dev/dri/card2"* ]] ||
  fail "a second NVIDIA card is not left out of the pin" "expected: '' or a list including /dev/dri/card2, actual: '$actual'"
pass "a second NVIDIA card is not left out of the pin"
```

Run from the repository root:

```
$ bash test/shell.d/hw-nvidia-drm-card-test.sh
ok - NVIDIA beside simpledrm is pinned, connectors are ignored
ok - any firmware framebuffer driver counts
ok - NVIDIA alone keeps autodetection
ok - a hybrid machine keeps autodetection
ok - a hybrid machine without a firmware framebuffer keeps autodetection
ok - no NVIDIA card keeps autodetection
ok - no DRM cards at all keeps autodetection
expected: '' or a list including /dev/dri/card2, actual: '/dev/dri/card1'
not ok - a second NVIDIA card is not left out of the pin
```

Exit status: 1.

Both suggested fixes pass this case and the file's existing seven cases:
- Count the NVIDIA cards and pin only when exactly one is present. The Lua configs stay unchanged, and two NVIDIA cards beside simpledrm set nothing.
- Collect every NVIDIA card and print them joined with `:`, which is safe because `/dev/dri/cardN` contains no colon. Widen the Lua match in both configs, for example to `match("^(/dev/dri/card[%d:/a-z]*)")`. Two NVIDIA cards beside simpledrm then set `AQ_DRM_DEVICES=/dev/dri/card1:/dev/dri/card2` in both the session and the greeter.
</details>

<details><summary>More findings: no test covers the Lua pin (test-only)</summary>

With `hl.env("AQ_DRM_DEVICES", card)` removed from both configs, the new test and `hw-nvidia-test.sh` still pass, and the new test ignores the helper's exit status. **Impact:** test coverage only, not a production defect; a later change that drops the pin would go unnoticed.

**Suggested change:** Give `hw-nvidia-test.sh` a fake DRM tree, print `AQ_DRM_DEVICES`, and add a greeter case. The `quattro` version of that test loads `nvidia.lua`; the version at the reviewed head does not, so this applies after a rebase.

**Reproducer (passes with the pin removed, at 11e7842):**

Reviewed head: `11e7842399030ad5affee4dc1214fb4272632e89`. The trial merge with `quattro` at `8b4eae66da2938ba9559f103b18dbf85cdf28a70` was also checked, because there `test/shell.d/hw-nvidia-test.sh` evaluates `default/hypr/nvidia.lua`.

Remove the pin from both configs, then run the new test and the existing NVIDIA test from the repository root.

```
$ sed -i 's/hl.env("AQ_DRM_DEVICES", card)/-- removed/' default/hypr/nvidia.lua default/sddm/hyprland.lua
$ bash test/shell.d/hw-nvidia-drm-card-test.sh
ok - NVIDIA beside simpledrm is pinned, connectors are ignored
ok - any firmware framebuffer driver counts
ok - NVIDIA alone keeps autodetection
ok - a hybrid machine keeps autodetection
ok - a hybrid machine without a firmware framebuffer keeps autodetection
ok - no NVIDIA card keeps autodetection
ok - no DRM cards at all keeps autodetection
```

Exit status: 0 at the head and on the trial merge.

`test/shell.d/hw-nvidia-test.sh` on the trial merge, with the same edit:

```
$ bash test/shell.d/hw-nvidia-test.sh
ok - AMD only
ok - NVIDIA audio only
ok - No PCI devices
ok - Turing (first GSP)
ok - Volta (last without GSP)
ok - Maxwell (first 580xx)
ok - Kepler (unsupported)
ok - AMD display with Ampere offload
ok - Intel display with Maxwell offload
ok - NVIDIA display with inactive iGPU
ok - Hybrid without boot_vga
```

Exit status: 0. At the head, this test file does not load `nvidia.lua` at all, and it also passes (exit 0).

The same trial-merge run of `hw-nvidia-test.sh` calls the new detector 8 times, and every call has `OMARCHY_DRM_CLASS_PATH` unset. On a developer machine, each call therefore reads the real `/sys/class/drm`. That does not change the test's result, because the test prints only `NVD_BACKEND`, `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME` and `__GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME`.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified**
- The detector pins NVIDIA beside simpledrm, efidrm, vesadrm and corebootdrm, and prints nothing (exit 1) for NVIDIA alone, hybrid machines and nouveau (16 synthetic sysfs cases).
- Hyprland 0.56.2 parses the Lua config before it creates the Aquamarine backend, so `hl.env` takes effect at startup. The value is recomputed on every parse, so renumbered cards cannot leave a stale pin across boots.
- `/dev/dri/cardN` has no `:`, which Aquamarine uses to split `AQ_DRM_DEVICES`.
- Session and greeter configs both set `/dev/dri/card1` in the target topology, and the greeter falls back to `/usr/share/omarchy` when `OMARCHY_PATH` is unset.
- The head merges into current `quattro` without conflicts, and the pin stays outside the NVIDIA display gate.

**Optional notes**
- `OMARCHY_DRM_PATH` already names the `/sys/class/drm` override (`bin/omarchy-hw-external-monitors`, its test, and several open PRs). Reusing it instead of the new `OMARCHY_DRM_CLASS_PATH` lets a test that fakes the DRM tree set one variable.
- When it pins, `hl.env` replaces an `AQ_DRM_DEVICES` the user already set, for example in `~/.config/uwsm/env-hyprland`. With one NVIDIA card that value can only name the same card, so this mainly matters with a second NVIDIA card. Skipping the pin when the variable is set would keep a deliberate user choice.
- On an NVIDIA-only machine with `nvidia_drm modeset=0` (not the Omarchy default), the NVIDIA card has no KMS, yet it is still pinned. Per Aquamarine source, it then finds no usable GPU instead of falling back to simpledrm (not run on hardware). Pinning only an NVIDIA card that has connector entries (`cardN-*`) would avoid that.

**Related open PRs:** #9483 and #7851 conflict with this PR in `default/hypr/nvidia.lua`. #6896, #10574 and #7501 conflict with it at the top of `default/sddm/hyprland.lua`, where both sides add code. #9063's debug warning about `/dev/dri/cardN` pins would also flag this computed pin.
</details>
